Chapter 3: Quadratic Equations

1. Definition
A quadratic equation in one unknown is an equation that can be written in the form
ax² + bx + c = 0 where a, b, c are real numbers and a ≠ 0.
The numbers a, b and c are called the coefficients of the equation.

Examples: 3x² − 5x + 2 = 0 (a = 3, b = −5, c = 2)
x² − 16 = 0 (a = 1, b = 0, c = −16)

2. The discriminant
The discriminant of the equation ax² + bx + c = 0 is the number
D = b² − 4ac

Rule (learn this by heart):
• If D > 0, the equation has two different solutions: x₁ = (−b − √D) / 2a and x₂ = (−b + √D) / 2a
• If D = 0, the equation has exactly one (repeated) solution: x = −b / 2a
• If D < 0, the equation has no real solution: S = { }

Always write the solution set as S = { … }.

Page 2

3. Special cases (no discriminant needed)
• If b = 0: ax² + c = 0 ⇔ x² = −c/a. Example: x² − 16 = 0 ⇔ x² = 16 ⇔ x = −4 or x = 4. S = {−4, 4}
• If c = 0: factorise out x. Example: 2x² − 8x = 0 ⇔ 2x(x − 4) = 0 ⇔ x = 0 or x = 4. S = {0, 4}

Warning: never divide both sides by x, you would lose the solution x = 0!

4. Sum and product of the solutions
If D ≥ 0: x₁ + x₂ = −b/a and x₁ · x₂ = c/a

EXERCISES

Ex 1. Solve over the real numbers:
a) x² − 7x + 10 = 0
b) 9x² − 12x + 4 = 0
c) 2x² + x + 3 = 0

Ex 1 answers (done in class)
a) D = 49 − 40 = 9; x₁ = (7 − 3)/2 = 2; x₂ = (7 + 3)/2 = 5; S = {2, 5}
b) D = 144 − 144 = 0; x = 12/18 = 2/3; S = {2/3}
c) D = 1 − 24 = −23 < 0; S = { }

Ex 2. Solve without using D:
a) 3x² − 48 = 0
b) 4x² + 10x = 0

Ex 2 answers
a) x² = 16 so S = {−4, 4}
b) 2x(2x + 5) = 0 so S = {0, −5/2}

Ex 3. Word problem. A rectangle is 3 cm longer than it is wide, and its area is 70 cm². What are its dimensions?
Answer: let w be the width, so w(w + 3) = 70, that is w² + 3w − 70 = 0. D = 9 + 280 = 289, √D = 17.
w = (−3 − 17)/2 = −10 or w = (−3 + 17)/2 = 7. A width cannot be negative.
Dimensions: 7 cm by 10 cm.

Ex 4. Without solving, give the sum and the product of the solutions of 3x² + 5x − 2 = 0.
(no answer given)
